source.title: Regularization by Misclassification in ReLU Neural Networks
source.authors: E. Cornacchia; Jan Hązła; Ido Nachum; A. Yehudayoff

record.file_problem: Full text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper examines training with random or corrupted labels. Its pure-noise results report network decay, while its partial-noise experiments report slower training and better test error in selected settings. It does not directly test whether standard networks fit a fixed random labeling to near-zero training error.
record.gate_note: Pure-label-noise results concern labels randomized independently at each training step, not a fixed random labeling of the training set. They measure weight decay or ReLU activity, not training error on random labels. The paper cites prior work on fitting random examples; those cited results are not extracted. Experiments comparing clean and noisy labels report selected settings, not a sweep over corruption rates.
record.test_reason: The study resamples label corruption independently at each SGD step, or uses label smoothing. Its results concern activation sparsity, network decay, and learning the original labels under these interventions. They do not test memorization of a fixed random or corrupted labeling, its optimization cost, or the ordering of signal learning and noise memorization.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: label noise or label smoothing induces sparser activation patterns across the studied settings, including MNIST and CIFAR-10; selected settings show improved generalization, and pure fresh label noise can cause network decay. These conclusions do not establish or refute memorization of fixed random labels.
record.recipe_differences: Studies stochastic label corruption or label smoothing, including fresh random labels at each SGD step and selected partial-noise settings. It does not use the fixed random-label fitting experiment described in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported pure-noise decay mode depends on bias neurons, input distribution, and learning rate. CIFAR-10 uses label smoothing; the authors state it produces denser representations than label noise.

fits_no_version.finding: On the hypercube task, fresh label noise with p = 0.2 slows reaching small training error while reducing test error from 49% to 21%; both regimes reach zero classification error on the original labels.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Resampling label noise during SGD can slow fitting of the original labels while improving generalization.

fits_no_version.finding: Fresh label noise improves MNIST test performance; CIFAR-10 label smoothing leaves reported accuracy similar, slightly above 92%. Both interventions produce sparser activations in these experiments.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Label noise or label smoothing can sparsify activations, with generalization benefits depending on the setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Pure, independently resampled label noise causes weight decay or ReLU death; the decay mode depends on bias terms, input distribution, and learning rate.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training ReLU networks under fresh random labels can cause network decay through distinct mechanisms.

record.problems: The partial-noise classification experiments compare only selected settings rather than a sweep of corruption rates. Some error curves are figure-only, and the paper gives no uncertainty estimates for the principal partial-noise comparisons. Pure-noise experiments do not report training error on a fixed random labeling.
record.rows_left_out: No additional numeric figure-only measurements were extracted for weight norms, active-neuron counts, or MNIST errors because exact values are not stated in the text. Figures 2–5 contain plots without recoverable numeric values in the supplied text.

untested.parts: Fitting a fixed completely random labeling to near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Training-time overhead for fitting fixed random labels and convergence trends across fixed corruption fractions. Slowing under fresh noise is a different comparison.
Perfect fitting of shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs. Gaussian inputs here accompany fresh random labels and norm measurements.
Perfect fitting of a fixed corrupted training set and steadily increasing test error across corruption fractions from zero to one.
Whether weight decay, dropout, and augmentation prevent fixed-random-label fitting, and whether removing them harms true-label generalization.
Learning shared real-data patterns before memorizing noisy labels and comparing real-label and random-label learning trajectories.

record.verdict_notes: The distinction is the corruption protocol, not merely the absence of a full corruption sweep or exact figure values. Independently resampled labels can conflict across presentations of the same input. Consequently, the extracted V2 and V4 verdicts should be removed. States marked cannot_determine refer to the claim versions, not to doubt about the reported norm, activity, or accuracy findings.

versions.untested_parts: The paper trains under fresh random labels and reports weight or activation decay, but does not report training error on a fixed, completely random labeling or test error at chance.
No small-constant-factor estimate, systematic corruption-rate sweep, or convergence-time scaling is reported.
Only selected noise settings are compared; the paper does not sweep corruption from none to all or report steadily rising test error across that range.

rows.subject: one hidden layer network with 4d neurons
rows.operation_detail: Train on the hypercube boundary function with label noise p = 0.2; compare with training without label noise.
rows.measure: Time to reach small training error
rows.baseline: without label noise: reaches zero classification error; exact time not stated
rows.value: with label noise: takes longer to reach small training error; exact time not stated
rows.note: The text says both networks are trained until zero classification error and longer afterward until test error stabilizes, but gives no time ratio.
rows.check: Remove V2: the comparison concerns repeatedly resampled label noise, not fitting a fixed corrupted labeling. Zero classification error is measured against the original dataset labels. Slower training is explicitly reported, but does not establish V2.

rows.subject: one hidden layer network with 4d neurons
rows.operation_detail: Train on the hypercube boundary function with label noise p = 0.2; compare with training without label noise.
rows.uncertainty: Plots averaged over 20 independent runs; no error bars stated
rows.note: This is one partial-noise comparison and does not measure a steady rise toward chance as corruption increases.
rows.check: Remove V4: 49% versus 21% test error compares clean training with fresh label corruption at each step. It does not measure generalization while memorizing a fixed corrupted training set. The numerical comparison is correctly extracted.

source_check.locator_found: Introduction, p. 2 (49% and 21%); Section 6.3, pp. 8–9; Figure 1 caption, p. 3 (20 independent runs).

rows.subject: one hidden layer network with 600 neurons
rows.operation_detail: Train on MNIST with label noise p = 0.1; compare with no label noise.

conditions.value: h = 0.01, decreased by factor 2 every 5 epochs

rows.baseline: Without label noise, the exact values are not stated.
rows.value: With label noise, the exact values are not stated; Figure 5b shows training and test classification errors.
rows.note: The text says the noisy-label network has better test performance, but does not give error values or report that both networks fit training labels perfectly.
rows.check: Remove V4: MNIST uses corruption resampled during training. The text explicitly reports better test performance with noise, although exact error values cannot be recovered from the supplied figure text.

rows.subject: ResNet-20
rows.size_stated: ResNet-20; penultimate layer consists of 4096 neurons
rows.operation_detail: Train on CIFAR-10 with label smoothing p = 0.1; compare with no label smoothing.
rows.baseline: Test accuracy slightly more than 92% without label smoothing
rows.value: Test accuracy slightly more than 92% with label smoothing
rows.note: Accuracy is reported as similar for the two settings; this is not a test-error sweep over corrupted-label fractions.
rows.check: Remove V4: label smoothing changes target distributions rather than assigning fixed random labels to examples. Similar accuracy slightly above 92% does not measure V4.

rows.subject: one hidden layer network with 4d neurons, no bias neurons
rows.operation_detail: Train under pure label noise over the normal distribution; report weight decay.
rows.note: This is a fresh random label at each step; the paper does not report training error on a fixed random labeling.
rows.check: Weight decay under independently sampled random labels is reported, but weight norms cannot establish fitting error on a fixed random labeling. The reported decay is a valid finding outside these versions.

rows.subject: one hidden layer network with bias neurons
rows.operation_detail: Train under pure label noise over the normal distribution; report ReLU activity and weight behavior.
rows.value: Weights do not decay to zero; all hidden ReLU neurons stop firing for almost all inputs from the distribution.
rows.note: This reports network decay under fresh random labels, not fitting error.
rows.check: ReLU death and nonvanishing weight norms under fresh random labels do not measure any claim version. The underlying finding is correctly extracted.

rows.subject: network with one hidden layer and 2k ReLU neurons
rows.operation_detail: Theorem 3: train only hidden weights with hinge loss under pure label noise.
rows.measure: Absolute network output on each input after training
rows.value: |N(x)| < 2kh for every x in D after a finite number of steps
rows.note: The theorem bounds output magnitude; it does not report training error or fitting of a fixed random labeling.
rows.check: The theorem bounds output magnitude under fresh random labels; it does not measure classification error or memorization of fixed labels. Specify hinge loss with beta = 0.

rows.subject: network with one hidden layer and 2k ReLU neurons
rows.operation_detail: Theorem 4: train only hidden weights with hinge loss under pure label noise at learning rate h ≥ 1.
rows.uncertainty: As k grows, with high probability
rows.note: The result concerns neuron death, not fitting a fixed random labeling.
rows.check: The theorem establishes hidden-neuron death under fresh random labels, not failure to memorize a fixed labeling. Specify hinge loss with beta = 0.

rows.subject: network with one hidden layer and 2k ReLU neurons
rows.operation_detail: Theorem 4: train only hidden weights with hinge loss under pure label noise at learning rate h ≤ 1/k.
rows.value: For all i, ReLU(W e_i) ≠ 0; at most k + o(k) coordinates are zero
rows.uncertainty: As k grows, with high probability
rows.note: This is a learning-rate-dependent activity result under fresh random labels.
rows.check: The theorem establishes surviving hidden activity under fresh random labels, not fitting of random labels. Specify hinge loss with beta = 0 and that the coordinate bound applies to each activation vector ReLU(W e_i).
